title: introduce cross-sdk SessionEnvelope and ergonomic streaming adapters; normalize auth/retry profiles; bump SDK versions
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We continue to see integration friction in customer apps when upgrading SDKs due to subtle differences in streaming ergonomics (cancel/peek semantics), credential reauth races, and inconsistent retry profiles across languages. This PR introduces a lightweight coordination primitive (SessionEnvelope) and a set of ergonomic streaming adapters to bring TypeScript/Python/Go behavior into near-parity while keeping the APIs minimal for client code.

Summary of changes: Adds a SessionEnvelope abstraction (server-agnostic session metadata + lease hint + heartbeat helper), normalizes retry profiles to RetryProfile v2 (backoff windows, jitter presets, idempotency hints), and exposes a new ergonomic async iterator surface with cancelable iteration and peek/cork hints. The PR also adds a small token refresh hook interface to avoid token-swap races during stream reconnects and introduces telemetry hooks for session lifecycle events. Finally, coordinate-version bumps were applied: typescript SDK -> v1.7.0, python SDK -> v0.9.4, go SDK -> v1.5.3 (minor).

Compatibility and migration notes: Default behavior is fully backward-compatible: old consumers keep existing flows. To opt into the ergonomic iterator, import `createCancelableStreamIterator()` and pass an optional SessionEnvelope from the credential provider. The token refresh hook is optional and defaults to the current refresh flow. RetryProfile v2 is selectable via a short feature flag (recommended for Dedicated workloads). Full migration steps are documented in the SDK changelogs and examples folder.

Checklist:
- [x] SessionEnvelope core and server contract docs
- [x] TS SDK ergonomic async iterator implementation and tests
- [x] Python shim to mirror iterator semantics (compat tests)
- [x] Go iterator facade and typed errors parity adjustments
- [x] Normalized RetryProfile v2 implementation and unit tests
- [x] Token refresh hook and integration tests with token rotation simulator
- [x] Bumped package.json / pyproject / go mod with versions and CHANGELOG excerpts

Why this is in redwood repo: Coordination touches generator templates and shared protocol docs that live in this repo; the SDK repos are version bumps that are published after merge. This PR stages the shape and tests across all three languages so downstream SDK releases can be fast and consistent.
